arxiv-2009-09205.title: Adversarial Rain Attack and Defensive Deraining for DNN Perception
arxiv-2009-09205.creator: Liming Zhai, Felix Juefei-Xu, Qing Guo, Xiaofei Xie, Lei Ma, Wei Feng, Shengchao Qin, and Yang Liu
arxiv-2009-09205.description: Abstract Rain often poses inevitable threats to deep neural network (DNN) based perception systems, and a comprehensive investigation of the potential risks of the rain to DNNs is of great importance. However, it is rather difficult to collect or synthesize rainy images that can represent all rain situations that would possibly occur in the real world.

arxiv-2103-13036.title: Skyrmion size in skyrmion crystals
arxiv-2103-13036.creator: H. T. Wu, X. C. Hu, K. Y. Jing, X. R. Wang
arxiv-2103-13036.description: Abstract A magnetic skyrmion is a topological object that can exist as a solitary embedded in the vast ferromagnetic phase, or coexists with a group of its “siblings” in various stripy phases as well as skyrmion crystals (SkXs). Isolated skyrmions and skyrmions in an SkX are circular while a skyrmion in other phases is a stripe of various forms.

arxiv-2212-10627.title: Asymptotic Fermat for signatures ( r , r , p ) (r,r,p) using the modular approach
arxiv-2212-10627.creator: Diana Mocanu
arxiv-2212-10627.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Diana Mocanu. Let K K be a totally real field, and r ≥ 5 r\geq 5 a fixed rational prime. In this paper, we use the modular method as presented in the recent work of Freitas and Siksek to study non-trivial, primitive solutions ( x , y , z ) ∈ 𝒪 K 3 (x,y,z)\in\mathcal{O}_{K}^{3} of the signature ( r , r , p ) (r,r,p) equation x r + y r = z p x^{r}+y^{r}=z^{p} (where p p is a prime that varies).

arxiv-2305-12439.title: Large shift current via in-gap and charge-neutral exciton excitations in BN nanotubes and single BN layer
arxiv-2305-12439.creator: Yi-Shiuan Huang 1, Yang-Hao Chan 2,3, Guang-Yu Guo 1,2
arxiv-2305-12439.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yi-Shiuan Huang 1, Yang-Hao Chan 2,3, Guang-Yu Guo 1,2. We perform ab initio many-body calculations to investigate the exciton shift current in small diameter zigzag BN nanotubes and also single BN sheet, using the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter equation (GW-BSE) method with the newly developed efficient algorithms. Our GW-BSE calculations reveal a giant in-gap peak in the shift current spectrum in all the studied BN systems due to the excitation of the A exciton.

arxiv-2312-06140.title: ICS-Sniper: A Targeted Blackhole Attack on Encrypted ICS Traffic
arxiv-2312-06140.creator: Gargi Mitra, Pritam Dash, Yingao Elaine Yao, Aastha Mehta, Karthik Pattabiraman
arxiv-2312-06140.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Gargi Mitra, Pritam Dash, Yingao Elaine Yao, Aastha Mehta, Karthik Pattabiraman. Operational Technology (OT) networks of industrial control systems (ICS) are increasingly connected to the public Internet, which has prompted ICSes to implement strong security measures (e.g., authentication and encryption) to protect end-to-end control communication. Despite the security measures, we show that an Internet adversary in the path of an ICS’s communication can cause damage to the ICS without infiltrating the ICS.

arxiv-2401-11114.title: DengueNet: Dengue Prediction using Spatiotemporal Satellite Imagery for Resource-Limited Countries
arxiv-2401-11114.creator: Kuan-Ting Kuo, Dana Moukheiber, Sebastian Cajas Ordonez, David Restrepo, Atika Rahman Paddo, Tsung-Yu Chen, Lama Moukheiber, Mira Moukheiber, Sulaiman Moukheiber, Saptarshi Purkayastha, Po-Chih Kuo, Leo Anthony Celi
arxiv-2401-11114.description: Abstract Dengue fever presents a substantial challenge in developing countries where sanitation infrastructure is inadequate. The absence of comprehensive healthcare systems exacerbates the severity of dengue infections, potentially leading to life-threatening circumstances. Rapid response to dengue outbreaks is also challenging due to limited information exchange and integration.

arxiv-2511-02453.title: Accounting for Underspecification in Statistical Claims of Model Superiority
arxiv-2511-02453.creator: Thomas Sanchez, Pedro Macias Gordaliza, Meritxell Bach Cuadra, [2mm] CIBM Center for Biomedical Imaging
arxiv-2511-02453.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Thomas Sanchez, Pedro Macias Gordaliza, Meritxell Bach Cuadra, [2mm] CIBM Center for Biomedical Imaging. Machine learning methods are increasingly applied in medical imaging, yet many reported improvements lack statistical robustness: recent works have highlighted that small but significant performance gains are highly likely to be false positives. However, these analyses do not take underspecification into account—the fact that models achieving similar validation scores may behave differently on unseen data due to random initialization or training dynamics.

pmc-10719019.title: Marine Collagen Matrix Carrier with Injectable Platelet-Rich Fibrin in Management of Gingival Recession Defects
pmc-10719019.creator: Deepikha Krishnaraj, Harinath Parthasarathy, Anupama Tadepalli, Deepa Ponnaaiyan, A. Thirumal Raj, Shankargouda Patil, Snehashish Ghosh
pmc-10719019.description: Background The gold standard in the management of gingival recession (GR) defects has been connective tissue graft (CTG) with coronally advanced flap (CAF). But patient morbidity associated with graft harvesting is a major drawback and has led to the development of various substitute biomaterials which have been tried and tested.

pmc-11434780.title: Role of Poly(A)-Binding Protein Cytoplasmic 1, a tRNA-Derived RNA Fragment-Bound Protein, in Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection
pmc-11434780.creator: Devin V. Davis, Eun-Jin Choi, Deena Ismail, Miranda L. Hernandez, Jong Min Choi, Ke Zhang, Kashish Khatkar, Sung Yun Jung, Wenzhe Wu, Xiaoyong Bao
pmc-11434780.description: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) is a significant cause of lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) across all demographics, with increasing mortality and morbidity among high-risk groups such as infants under two years old, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals. Although newly approved vaccines and treatments have substantially reduced RSV hospitalizations, accessibility remains limited, and response to treatment varies.

pmc-12382291.title: Understanding the traits underlying vaccine-driven virulence evolution in malaria parasites
pmc-12382291.creator: Youngseo Jeong, Tsukushi Kamiya, Nicole Mideo
pmc-12382291.description: BackgroundVaccine-driven evolution can erode the beneficial effects of vaccination and is a concern, especially for newly introduced vaccines. While obvious candidates for vaccine-driven evolution are the precise parasite antigens that are the targets of vaccine-induced immunity, traits underlying parasite virulence may also evolve.

pmc-12464706.title: Protocol for genomic surveillance of Plasmodium falciparum antigens using amplicon-based PacBio long-read sequencing
pmc-12464706.creator: David Fernando Plaza
pmc-12464706.description: SummaryHere, we present a protocol that identifies and classifies structurally diverse variants of msp1, msp2, glurp, and csp in Plasmodium falciparum using an amplicon-based long-read sequencing platform. We describe steps for PCR barcoding, PacBio circular consensus sequencing (CCS), in silico PCR-based size variant calling, and advanced data analysis in Galaxy.

pmc-12567568.title: Oncogenic Viruses in Organ Transplantation: Implications of Virus-Host Interactions for Cancer Development
pmc-12567568.creator: Seyed-Mahmood Seyed-Khorami, Arezou Azadi, Ala Habibian, Monireh Hosseini, Xiaofeng Fan, Hoorieh Soleimanjahi, Mahmoud Reza Pourkarim
pmc-12567568.description: Organ transplantation significantly enhances the survival and quality of life for recipients. However, multiple dependent and independent variables can adversely affect life expectancy after transplantation. Cancer is one of the most common causes of morbidity and mortality for long-term organ transplant recipients. The incidence of cancer in transplanted tissues can be twice as high in approximately 32 distinct cancer types.

pmc-12956263.title: CLINICAL EFFECTIVENESS OF ENDOSCOPIC SUBMUCOSAL DISSECTION IN THE MANAGEMENT OF SUPERFICIAL ESOPHAGEAL NEOPLASMS ASSOCIATED WITH BARRETT’S ESOPHAGUS
pmc-12956263.creator: Rúbia Moresi VIANNA DE OLIVEIRA, Josué ALIAGA RAMOS, Jonathan Richard WHITE, Vitor Nunes ARANTES
pmc-12956263.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: The main clinical impact of superficial neoplasms associated with Barrett’s esophagus lies in their increasing oncogenic potential in the medium and long term. For this reason, the main international guidelines agree on the importance of their early eradication. However, controversy persists as to the most appropriate endoscopic resection technique either endoscopic mucosal resection or endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) that guarantees the best resective quality standards.

uslaw-usc-t36-s40111.title: 36 U.S.C. § 40111 — Liability for acts of officers and agents
uslaw-usc-t36-s40111.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t36-s40111.description: United States Code, Title 36 (Patriotic And National Observances, Ceremonies, And Organizations); Part B (Organizations); Chapter 401 (Catholic War Veterans Of The United States Of America, Incorporated). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The corporation is liable for the acts of its officers and agents acting within the scope of their authority.
